summary: Forestry Division tower begun north of Jay in 1957 on land local people donated; the last report found is May 1958, so its fate is unknown.

events.note: Construction began in 1957: surveyors plotted the site by late October, footing holes were being dug in November. The May 1958 report had the tower at about 60 ft and still going up. No completion date found.

evidence.supports: Jay tower is a Forestry Division fire tower; announced July 1957
evidence.quote: Location of a Forestry Division fire tower near Jay was announced today by Senator J.R. Hall and Representative Wiley Sparkman.

evidence.supports: Delaware County
evidence.quote: Delaware County

evidence.supports: Coverage to Ottawa County and other county towers, as the Journal reported
evidence.quote: will give the division coverage from here to Ottawa county and coverage to the other towers already in the county

evidence.supports: Committee first chose the city park, hoping for a tourist attraction
evidence.quote: designated the city park as a location of the tower which will become a tourist attraction

evidence.supports: Drop in elevation made the park site not feasible
evidence.quote: a drop in elevation made this not feasible

evidence.supports: New site selected, awaiting division approval
evidence.quote: The committee has selected a new site, tentatively, and now are awaiting the approval of the division.

evidence.supports: Tower located north of Jay on land formerly owned by Wick Francis
evidence.quote: The tower is located North of Jay on the ground formerly owned by Wick Francis.

evidence.supports: Ten Jay business people bought the land; half donated to the state
evidence.quote: The land was recently purchased by 10 Jay business people, and half the tract donated to the state for the tower site.

evidence.supports: Division to develop a public park alongside the tower
evidence.quote: The division will take the acreage and develop a park for public use in addition to maintaining the fire lookout tower.

evidence.supports: Planned height about 100 feet
evidence.quote: Indications are the tower will reach approximately 100 feet into the sky

evidence.supports: Surveyors plotted the site in October 1957
evidence.quote: surveyors plotted the site for locations of the tower and buildings

evidence.supports: Footing holes being dug; wet weather slowing work (November 1957)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 30.5 m matches the 100 ft planned in 1957. The May 1958 report gave about 60 ft during construction, and no completed height was found. Height is left out of facts.

sources.title: Oklahoma State Forestry History
sources.publisher: Oklahoma Department of Agriculture, Food, and Forestry

notes_for_editor: Only 1957-58 newspaper reports (quoted on the Forest Lookouts page) date this tower; the Delaware County Journal itself was not readable (newspapers.com returned 403). No source after May 1958 was found, so status and access are unknown and left out of facts. Staffing is not stated beyond district rangers overseeing construction, so it is left out. Record height_m 30.5 is the planned height, not a verified as-built height. Neither the Oklahoma NHLR nor FFLOS index pages in the local crawl list Jay.
